newsitem.title: USA: Western Resources buying Kansas City P&L.
newsitem.headline: Western Resources buying Kansas City P&L.

text.p: Western Resources Inc. will buy Kansas City Power & Light Co. in a $2 billion stock swap, the two companies announced Friday, in the first hostile takeover of a U.S. utility.

Under the tax-free deal approved by both companies' boards, Kansas City, Mo.-based Kansas City Power shareholders will receive $32 worth of Topeka, Kan.-based Western Resources' common stock for each share they hold.

Kansas City Power's surrender ended a 10-month battle in which UtiliCorp United Inc., also headquartered in Kansas City, saw its friendly pact to merge with Kansas City fall apart after shareholders in September rejected that proposed $1.7 billion deal.
Analysts have said the merger of Western Resources and Kansas City Power would create a Midwestern electric and natural gas powerhouse better poised to compete in the deregulating utility business.
The merged company will have nearly $3 billion in annual revenues and nearly 2.5 million gas and electric customers. Western Resources also has 430,000 security customers.

"... This combination will create value for shareowners and choices for customers as we position ourselves to be a premier energy and security provider throughout the nation," Kansas City Power Chairman Drue Jennings said in a statement.
Jennings said the deal was expected to save $1 billion over 10 years, but said both companies had promised no employees would be laid off as a result of the merger.
"Anyone who wants to stay with the new company will have an opportunity to do so," Western Resources Chairman John Hayes told reporters in a telephone conference call after the statement.
Jennings and Hayes said they had put behind them any bad feelings resulting from the takeover struggle that began last April.
"The process of merging our companies has been long and, at times, trying. Today, we are putting the past behind us and we are ready to plan our future," Hayes said.
Under the deal, Hayes will remain chairman and chief executive of the new company while Jennings will become vice chairman and be responsible for electric utility operations.
Kansas City Power will continue to have its own board and will retain its current headquarters, the companies said.

Jennings said the turning point in negotiations came when Western Resources began reshaping itself as more than just an electric utility by buying the monitored security business of Westinghouse Electric Corp. and by launching an unsolicited $3.5 billion bid for electronic security giant ADT Ltd.

"Frankly, at the time we began our merger discussions with UtiliCorp, Western Resources appeared to us to be quite a traditional utility company," Jennings said. "But things have changed and they've changed dramatically.

Hayes said he thought the proposed merger would not have any difficulty meeting the new tougher merger guidelines adopted by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. He said he expected to receive regulatory approval of the merger within 12 months.

In addition to the commission, the deal is subject to approval by both companies' shareholders, utility regulatory bodies in Missouri and Kansas and the federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission, the companies said.
Kansas City Power stock rose 37.5 cents to $29.125, but Western Resources stock dropped 25 cents to $30.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
